content.text:
Removed the mobile burger menu from `apps/web/app/[locale]/components/navbar.tsx:1`.

**What went:**
- `MobileNavButton` (the burger) and `MobileNav` (the empty panel it opened)
- The `open`/`toggleMobileNav` state, and with it `useState`/`useCallback` and the `Menu` icon import
- The `"use client"` directive — nothing left in the file needs the client, so the navbar is now a server component (small bundle win, in the spirit of the recent Lighthouse work)

**What stayed:** `DesktopNav` and the empty `links` array, so re-adding nav links later is a one-line change. It renders an empty `<nav>` on desktop today, same as before.

**Verified:** Biome clean, `tsc --noEmit` on `apps/web` clean, 198/198 web tests pass, and I loaded the page at 390×844 in Chrome — header shows the logo only, no burger. (Root `bun test` shows 1 failure, the known BSON `ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` false failure unrelated to this change.)
commit and push, open a PR. By the way, update your memory to your default behavior which I believe is to commit regularly.

---
name: feedback-commit-regularly
description: On hasToggle, commit finished work without being asked — the default is regular commits, not a clean tree waiting for permission
metadata:
  type: feedback
---
On hasToggle, commit work as it finishes rather than leaving it uncommitted until Eric asks. A verified, self-contained change (checks clean, tests pass) is a commit — don't wait for a "commit this" instruction. Push and open a PR when a branch's work is done.

**Why:** Eric stated on 2026-08-20 that regular committing is the expected default. Sessions here move through many small verified units (a copy edit, a demo migration, a perf fix), and holding them in the working tree makes the history less useful and risks losing a coherent unit to a later, unrelated edit.

**How to apply:** After the verification gate passes (`bun run check`, `tsc --noEmit`, the app's `bun test` — see [[project-env-quirks]] for the root-suite false failures), commit that unit with a real message. Stage only the files the change touched — planning artifacts stay untracked per [[feedback-no-commit-artifacts]], and stray untracked files from other tooling are not yours to commit. Ask before pushing to a shared branch or force-pushing; ordinary commits on a feature branch need no permission.
